classes.definition: A reported numeric value differs from the governing evidence value.
A rate or share uses or calculates the wrong denominator.
A currency, scale, measurement, or magnitude unit materially changes a source value.
Eligible, non-overlapping evidence values are combined incorrectly.
Multiple records for one governed identity are counted as distinct objects.
The wrong earliest or latest eligible record is selected from a complete set.
A repository, publication, or processing date is substituted for the requested event chronology.
A missing date is invented or inferred without an authorized evidence rule.
A timestamp is assigned to the wrong required local calendar date or time.
An explicit inclusive or exclusive interval endpoint is handled incorrectly.
Evidence outside the requested period is included or eligible in-period evidence is excluded.
Proposed, draft, scheduled, recommended, or incomplete activity is reported as final or completed.
A stated inclusion rule is not applied consistently to the evidence set.
A stale record is treated as current despite an explicit correction or supersession.
Similar names or nearby records are substituted despite stable identity evidence.
A statement is assigned to a person or role the retained evidence does not identify.
An unresolved pronoun, referent, or identity is selected as fact.
Lower-authority, indirect, preliminary, or superseded evidence is preferred over the governing source.
An attached evidence locator does not support the material claim associated with it.
An explicit material-claim locator requirement is unmet.
A material population, condition, exception, or limitation in the evidence is removed.
Possibility, compatibility, or bounded evidence is restated as proof or exclusion.
Association or before/after evidence is converted into a causal conclusion.
Genuinely insufficient evidence is converted into a determinate conclusion.
A partial or unenumerated evidence sample is declared complete.
A bounded or incomplete negative search is treated as proof of universal absence.
Matching evidence is present but the answer says it is absent.
An evaluative category lacks a supplied governing threshold or boundary.
Material claims within the submitted answer cannot all be true together.
Available contrary evidence that changes the conclusion is excluded from the synthesis.
Truncation, negation loss, or context removal changes a source statement's meaning.
A material proposition is directly contradicted by governed evidence without a more specific class.
